questions.prompt: Mina tells her cousin how she likes to go to Italy. Which sentence is correct?

options.text: I prefer to travelling by boat.
I prefer to travel by boat.

questions.explanation: Prefer takes to plus the bare verb (I prefer to travel) or the verb with -ing (I prefer travelling), never the two together and never the bare verb alone. The boat is a vehicle, so it takes by: the sentence with to in front of the boat puts the word of the place where the word of the vehicle belongs.

questions.prompt: In which country do people throw tomatoes at each other during a summer festival?
questions.explanation: The festival where people throw tomatoes at each other for one morning is La Tomatina, and it is a custom of Spain. Egypt is the country of the pyramids, China of the Great Wall, and Japan of the bow that greets people.

questions.prompt: The Eiffel Tower is 330 metres high, the Great Pyramid of Giza 139 metres and the tower of Big Ben 96 metres. Which sentence is correct?

options.text: The Eiffel Tower is taller than the three.
The Eiffel Tower is the tallest of the three.
The Great Pyramid is the tallest of the three.
Big Ben is the tallest of the three.

questions.explanation: 330 metres is more than 139 and more than 96, so the Eiffel Tower stands above the whole group and takes the superlative: it is the tallest of the three. Saying taller than the three uses the tool for two things only, and the two other sentences give the first place to a shorter monument.

options.text: We travelled by Italy by boat.
We travelled by Italy to boat.
We travelled to Italy by boat.
We travelled to Italy to boat.

questions.explanation: Sort the two little words by what follows them: Italy is a place, so it takes to, and a boat is a vehicle, so it takes by. Only We travelled to Italy by boat puts each word where it belongs; the others send the traveller by a country or to a vehicle.

questions.prompt: Complete: "In Seville I watched ___ flamenco dancer, and ___ dancer wore a long red dress."
questions.explanation: The dancer is new for your reader when she first appears, and the word flamenco begins with a consonant, so she arrives with a; the second time she is already known, so she takes the. Starting with an would need a vowel after it, and starting with the would point at somebody the reader has never met.

questions.prompt: Complete with the adjective easy: "This road is ___ that one."
questions.explanation: Easy ends in a consonant plus -y, so the y becomes i before the ending: easier than. The spelling easyer keeps the y the rule changes, more never joins a short adjective, and the ending -est needs a whole group and refuses than.
